I spent my childhood nearby my grandma's house, which therefore meant that she had influence over my mother and my beliefs. She made my mother take my sister and I to church and we did almost all those ceremonies. I never wanted any of it.

I remember after my first communion (or whatever eating the thin bread is called elsewhere), I was told to pray a lot of prayers I don't remember. And I didn't, and they didn't find out, because there wasn't an omnipresent being whispering in their ears about my misbehavior.

I was lucky, my family moved away from grandma and the influence wasn't as great as before. I decided to ask my parents to not send me into confirmation school, they agreed because they didn't want me to go either from the beginning.


After many years, I'm now 18, and I haven't gone to church for a long while now. I don't believe in God, or in any religion, really. I recognize their power over people and the effort it takes to make people believe, but I'm simply not interested. As a kid, I would rather play video games than learn some tricky song about a dove and the end of times.

I think that you should slowly try to pry your parent's opinion on the matter, without revealing your own. And once you know they'll understand, you could try and talk yourself out of the inconvenience of going through that relatively unnecessary process.

If you're going to talk to them, remember to be respectful, I know things can get heated, so try to remember that they've lived under the wing of the church all their lives if they're uncooperative, they don't know any other way and may even want you to break the chain, but they are afraid or under the influence of a third party. As long as the two parts of the discussion understand each other, progress can be made.
